title: 6.9.6 Lab: Find the start
description: The maze is built, but the player always stands at a fixed spot in the corridor instead of on the P in the map. Scan the map for the P, turn its row and column into pixels, put the player there, and write the way back from pixels to a tile.

steps.title: Scan for P
steps.instructions: The starter has the maze from 6.9.4, the player standing at a fixed spot (220, 60) in the top corridor, and an empty `findStart(map)` that gives back the top-left tile for now. Write the scan inside `findStart(map)`, above the last line. Use two loops, one inside the other: `r` over the rows (`map.length`) and, inside it, `c` over the letters of that row (`map[r].length`). When `map[r][c]` is `'P'`, `return` an object `{ x, y }` holding the pixel centre of that tile: the centre of column `c` is `c * TILE + TILE / 2`, and the centre of row `r` is `r * TILE + TILE / 2`, as in 6.9.5. To join the two pieces of 6.9.5: the coin counter's `if (map[r][c] === 'c') { ... }` sat inside both loops, and `return { x: 60, y: 60 }` handed back two numbers. Here the `if` asks about `'P'`, and the braces hold a `return` of an object whose two 60s are replaced by the pixel formulas. Nothing changes on screen until step 2 uses it.
hints: The scan is `for (let r = 0; r < map.length; r++) { for (let c = 0; c < map[r].length; c++) { ... } }`, the nested loops of 6.9.5.
`if (map[r][c] === 'P') { return { x: c * TILE + TILE / 2, y: r * TILE + TILE / 2 }; }` goes inside the inner loop. The `x` comes from the column and the `y` from the row.

steps.title: Start there
steps.instructions: In `setup()`, the last lines of the starter are comments for this step. Ask `findStart(map)` for the start with `const start = findStart(map);`, then put the player on it: `player.x = start.x;` and `player.y = start.y;`. Run it: the blue square should stand on the spot the P marks, one tile in from the top-left corner, instead of at the fixed spot further along the corridor.
hints: `const start = findStart(map);` gives you an object, and `start.x` and `start.y` are its two numbers.
`player.x = start.x;` and then the same line for `y`. Both go in `setup()`, after the player is made.

steps.title: Pixels back to a tile
steps.instructions: Write `tileAt(x, y)`, the way back from pixels to a tile. Make `const c = floor(x / TILE);` for the column and `const r = floor(y / TILE);` for the row, then `return map[r][c];`. Use `floor`, not `round`: `floor` gives the tile the pixel is inside. The second line of words, under `coins left`, reads `standing on: [undefined]` until `tileAt` gives something back, and should now show the letter under the player. Walk to the first coin and read that line: it should say `[c]` when you stand on it, and `[ ]` on open floor.
hints: The row comes from `y` and the column from `x`. Say it as 'row first, then column' when you read the map: `map[r][c]`.
If the corner says `[c]` where there is no coin, you probably swapped `r` and `c`: walk to the first coin and check.

requirements.title: findStart looks at every letter of every row
requirements.description: Two loops, one inside the other: rows, then the letters of each row. Help: 6.9.5 (Reading: Reading a map as data)

requirements.title: It looks for the letter P
requirements.description: The scan stops at the tile that holds P. Help: 6.9.5 (Reading: Reading a map as data)

requirements.title: Row and column become pixels
requirements.description: A tile centre is its column (or row) times TILE, plus half a tile. Writing it out, or calling the cellToPixel helper from 5.13.2, both count. Help: 6.9.5 (Reading: Reading a map as data)

requirements.title: The player is put on the start
requirements.description: setup asks findStart for the start and moves the player there. Help: 6.9.5 (Reading: Reading a map as data)

requirements.title: tileAt turns pixels into a row and a column with floor
requirements.description: floor(x / TILE) is the column, floor(y / TILE) is the row, and the answer is map[row][col]. Help: 6.9.5 (Reading: Reading a map as data)
